title: pause - treat a tty with no controlling terminal as non interactive
body:
##### SUMMARY

`Display.prompt_until()` determines whether stdin is interactive by comparing `os.getpgrp()` against `os.tcgetpgrp(self._stdin_fd)`. When stdin is a tty that has no controlling terminal (for example, a pty allocated by `docker run -t` without a session leader/`TIOCSCTTY`, as commonly happens in CI runners and Molecule/Docker test harnesses), `os.tcgetpgrp()` raises `OSError` (`ENOTTY`, errno 25) instead of returning normally.

That exception was unhandled and propagated all the way up as a raw task failure:
```
[Errno 25] Inappropriate ioctl for device
```

instead of being treated like any other non-interactive stdin, which normally produces a clean `AnsiblePromptNoninteractive` and, for `pause`, a `[WARNING]: Not waiting for response to prompt as stdin is not interactive` message instead of a failure.

This PR catches `OSError` from `tcgetpgrp()` and treats it the same as running in the background, matching the existing non interactive handling.

A regression unit test (`test_Display_prompt_until_tty_without_controlling_terminal`) was added that mocks `os.tcgetpgrp` to raise `OSError(errno.ENOTTY, ...)` and asserts `AnsiblePromptNoninteractive` is raised instead of the exception propagating.

**Verified:**
- New unit test passes on Python 3.13/3.14/3.15.
- `ansible-test sanity` is clean on all changed files.
- The full `ansible-test units` suite (Python 3.9-3.15) passes with no regressions.

This PR closes #85703.

##### ISSUE TYPE

- Bugfix Pull Request
